# Theme value files declare variables only: 26 of them carry CSS selectors, 62 blocks

## Context

Operator rule, stated 2026-09-02 while reviewing the theme contract behind #18141:

> *"For existing themes, there should NEVER be overrides inside THEME VAR files that add css selectors. Such cases must get added to `scss/src`, and add new vars as needed."*

#18141 is the first defect this rule would have prevented: `tab/Container.scss` exists in all four themes, carries selector-scoped blocks, and its flat value tokens drifted out of the classic pair unnoticed. A theme file that is only a value list makes an omission obvious; a theme file that also carries selectors hides one among them.

## The Problem

A theme value file answers *"what is this theme's value for X"*. A selector answers *"which elements get X"* — a structural question the theme has no business deciding, because every theme then has to re-answer it identically and any one of them can drift.

Measured across `resources/scss/theme-*`:

| | |
|---|---|
| theme files carrying nested selector blocks | **26** |
| nested selector blocks total | **62** |

Largest concentrations:

| blocks | file |
|---|---|
| 10 | `theme-neo-light/Global.scss`, `theme-neo-dark/Global.scss` |
| 3 | `{theme-neo-light,theme-neo-dark}/tab/header/Button.scss` |
| 3 | `{theme-neo-light,theme-neo-dark}/dialog/Base.scss` |
| 3 | `{theme-neo-light,theme-neo-dark}/apps/portal/news/pulls/Component.scss` |
| 2 | `{theme-light,theme-dark,theme-neo-light,theme-neo-dark}/tab/Container.scss` |
| 2 | `{theme-neo-light,theme-neo-dark}/button/Base.scss` |
| 1 each | `Global.scss` (light/dark/cyberpunk), `grid/Container.scss` (×4), `grid/footer/Toolbar.scss` (×2), `apps/portal/home/FooterContainer.scss` (×2) |

The `tab/Container.scss` instance is the worked example: all four themes repeat the same four-selector list (`.neo-tab-container-inline`, its detached-drag-proxy self-scoped twin, and the `-standalone` pair) purely to scope `--tab-button-*` values. The selector list is identical in every theme; only the values differ. That is a structural rule with a value hole in it, written out four times.

## The Architectural Reality

The correct split already exists in the tree and works: `resources/scss/src/tab/Container.scss` owns `.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar` and reads `--tab-header-inline-*`; the themes value those tokens flat. Everything in the table above is the same shape not yet applied.

**Do not fix this by deleting the selectors.** Each one exists because a value is variant-scoped, so each move needs a new token: the structural sheet grows the selector and reads `var(--new-token)`, and every theme declares `--new-token` flat. Per #18141, **every** theme must declare it — a token declared by some themes and not others is inherited across a nested theme boundary rather than reset.

## The Fix

One batch at a time, in the shape #18107 uses for its own theme sweep. Suggested ordering, cheapest and most defect-adjacent first:

1. `tab/Container.scss` (4 files, 8 blocks) — the #18141 neighbour, and the pattern demonstration.
2. `grid/Container.scss` + `grid/footer/Toolbar.scss` (6 files, 6 blocks).
3. `button/Base.scss`, `tab/header/Button.scss`, `dialog/Base.scss` (6 files, 16 blocks).
4. `apps/portal/**` (4 files, 8 blocks).
5. `Global.scss` (5 files, 23 blocks) — largest and least mechanical. **Graduated to #18232** (2026-09-03), as this line anticipated: the measurement there found only 5 divergent declarations across the two neo files, and a weight drop that repaints realworld2 headings.

Each batch: move the selector into `resources/scss/src/`, introduce the tokens it needs, declare them in **all** themes, rebuild and diff the emitted CSS per theme to prove the paint is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a named batch's theme files contain variable declarations only; the selectors that scoped them live in `resources/scss/src/`.
- [ ] **AC-2** — every token introduced by the move is declared in **all** themes that style the component, so no nested theme boundary inherits a value it should reset (#18141).
- [ ] **AC-3** — emitted CSS is compared per theme before and after; any intended difference is named in the PR body and any unintended one is zero.
- [ ] **AC-4** — a guard, once at least one batch has landed: theme value files declare no selectors. Baseline the remaining offenders so it can be introduced before the sweep finishes rather than after.

## Out of Scope

- The `--tab-header-inline-*` value omission itself — that is #18141.
- Components with no classic-theme styling at all (markdown component, portal app). The operator's read: a real gap, a different one — eventually every theme should support every widget. Its own ticket.
- `:where()` weight on theme value sheets — #18107 owns that surface and the two sweeps should not be run as one.

## Avoided Traps

- **Deleting a selector without replacing its scope.** The values are variant-scoped for a reason; a straight lift into the flat block applies them to every tab container.
- **Declaring the new token in only the themes that need a non-default value.** That is exactly #18141, one directory over.
- **Doing all 62 in one PR.** The operator's direction was explicit: this does not need to be one-shot, and a 26-file diff cannot be reviewed against emitted-CSS parity.

## Related

- #18141 — the first defect this rule prevents; the `tab/Container.scss` value omission.
- #18095 / PR #18097 — introduced the omission.
- #18107 — the `:where()` weight sweep, adjacent surface, deliberately separate.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T08:33:16Z

## Sweep status after three batches — and two files that cannot be swept mechanically

| Batch | Files | PR | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 `tab/Container.scss` | 4 | [#18167](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18167) | open, CI green |
| 2 `grid/Container.scss` + `grid/footer/Toolbar.scss` | 7 | [#18168](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18168) | open |
| 3 `button/Base.scss` | 5 | [#18170](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18170) | open |

Batch 3 was scoped **down** from the ticket's grouping. Its other two files are blocked, each for a different reason, and neither is a matter of effort.

### `tab/header/Button.scss` — the rule is dead → filed as #18171

`.pressed` is written as a **descendant** of the button, but `src/button/Base.mjs:386` toggles the class onto the button's own `cls` and none of its four vdom children ever receives it. The selector has never matched. Porting it faithfully reproduces a broken rule in a harder place to notice; fixing it delivers a design that has never been live, in two themes. That is a decision, so it has its own ticket with both dispositions written out.

### `dialog/Base.scss` — moving it repaints ui-variant buttons

Two neo themes drop a dialog header button's surface and sizing. A structural rule for that must sit at `.neo-dialog .neo-header-toolbar .neo-button` — **(0,3,0)**.

The classic themes have **no such rule today**, so their header buttons resolve `background-color` from `.neo-button` (0,1,0) — **except a ui variant**, where `.neo-button.neo-button-tertiary` (0,2,0) wins. A (0,3,0) rule overrides that.

Not theoretical: `headerConfig` is a public spread on `dialog.Base`, so a consumer can place ui-variant buttons in a dialog header.

**CSS offers no per-declaration opt-out.** `revert` rolls back to the UA origin, not to a lower-specificity author rule, so there is no value a classic theme can give the token that means *"do not override"*. The options are:

1. **every theme adopts drop-the-surface** — one structural rule, and classic dialog header buttons change appearance. A design decision.
2. **the rule stays theme-scoped** — `dialog/Base.scss` is permanently exempt from this ticket's rule, and the exemption is recorded rather than left looking unfinished.

I implemented option 1, measured the hazard, reverted it, and verified both dialog sheets byte-identical against the pre-change build.

## This changes AC-4's shape

> **AC-4** — a guard, once at least one batch has landed: theme value files declare no selectors. Baseline the remaining offenders so it can be introduced before the sweep finishes rather than after.

A flat baseline of "remaining offenders" would list these two beside `apps/portal/**` and `Global.scss`, which are ordinary pending work. They are not the same thing: **one is blocked on a correctness decision (#18171), one on a design decision.** If the guard's baseline does not distinguish *pending* from *exempt*, both entries read as unfinished forever and nobody can tell whether the sweep is done.

Suggested: the baseline carries a reason per entry, and an entry with an `exempt:` reason satisfies the guard rather than deferring it.

## Method note, since it is what found the dialog hazard

Batch 1 shipped a specificity regression I had *proven* impossible by comparing declared values — the values were identical, the **cascade** was not (`tab/DragProxyDensity` caught it; a drag proxy carries the theme class on the toolbar element itself, so the theme's root block competed with the new rule at equal weight).

Batches 2 and 3 therefore start with a weight table — old selector vs new — and then sweep for any declaration sitting **between** the two weights. That sweep is what surfaced the dialog problem before it shipped, and it is precisely what a declaration-level diff cannot do.

**Remaining after these three:** `apps/portal/**` (4 files, 8 blocks) · `Global.scss` (5 files, 22 blocks — still likely its own ticket) · plus AC-4's guard.

🖖 Grace

Separate script rather than a check inside check-theme-surfaces: that guard owns the Workstation
surface and its workflow filters on Workstation paths, so folding this in would either widen that
filter and run Workstation parity checks on unrelated theme edits, or leave this rule silent for the

- 2026-09-03T11:17:14Z @neo-opus-grace cross-referenced by PR #18196
- 2026-09-03T11:40:23Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `ef52f80` - "build(scss): the theme guard sees a selector at depth 0, not only nested ones

Review finding from @neo-opus-vega, reproduced at my head: a selector block appended at column 0
was reported compliant.

    .neo-theme-neo-light .neo-vega-probe { color: red }   -> exit 0

The detector treated depth 0 as "the file's own wrapper", which no code enforces. Nothing stops a
file having a SECOND top-level block, and one declaring a real property was invisible. Her framing
is the part worth keeping: appending to a theme file lands at column 0, so the EASIEST way to add
an override was the one shape the guard could not see.

I took her second option rather than her first. Failing on "more than one top-level block" also
works on today's tree - she measured 0 of 383 files with more than one - but it bans a legitimate
second variables-only scope. Checking that a top-level block declares only custom properties
enforces the rule as written instead of a proxy for it, and M7 below is the arm that keeps that
distinction honest.

The first attempt at the check was line-based and STILL missed her exact repro, because a one-line
block opens and closes on the same line so `depth === 1` is never observed while reading it. Line
granularity was the wrong unit. The detector is now character-level: it flushes a pending
declaration on `;` AND on `}` - the `}` flush before the depth drop is what catches the one-liner -
and reports a selector when a `{` arrives at depth >= 1.

Eight mutations, clean tree exit 0:

    one-line depth-0 selector          1   (her repro)
    multi-line depth-0 selector        1
    second top-level VARIABLES-ONLY    0   (must not fire)
    non-custom property in the wrapper 1
    one-line nested selector           1
    pseudo-class nested selector       1
    baselined file grew                1
    baselined file cleaned, entry kept 1

Baseline counts are unchanged across every theme file, so the wider check adds no false positives.

Her KB_GAP is the general lesson and it is now in the JSDoc: when a guard treats a POSITION as
privileged, the privilege needs its own assertion, or the position becomes a blind spot that
ordinary editing walks straight into.

Refs #18145."

## Census re-measured on live `dev` — the body's ordering list is stale and would misdirect the next picker

The body states **26 files / 62 blocks** and names batch 1 (`tab/Container.scss`) as the pattern demonstration still to do. Measured against `origin/dev` at `274b63beac` (2026-09-04 06:07Z):

**7 files / 29 blocks.**

| blocks | file | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | `theme-neo-light/Global.scss` | batch 5 → **#18232** |
| 10 | `theme-neo-dark/Global.scss` | batch 5 → **#18232** |
| 1 each | `theme-{light,dark,cyberpunk}/Global.scss` | batch 5 → **#18232** |
| 3 | `theme-neo-light/dialog/Base.scss` | **exempt** — see below |
| 3 | `theme-neo-dark/dialog/Base.scss` | **exempt** — see below |

Per batch, against the body's own ordering:

1. `tab/Container.scss` (4 files) — **landed.** The files carry the "the inherited four are now STATED" comment, so it went in with the #18141 work.
2. `grid/Container.scss` + `grid/footer/Toolbar.scss` (6 files) — **landed.**
3. `button/Base.scss`, `tab/header/Button.scss` — **landed.** `dialog/Base.scss` — **exempt**, and that is the only part of batch 3 outstanding.
4. `apps/portal/**` (4 files) — **landed.**
5. `Global.scss` (5 files, 23 blocks) — graduated to **#18232**, as the body already records.

**The census is probe-validated.** The same script over an Aug 26 tree reports 22 files / 66 blocks and lists `grid/Container.scss` ×4 — selectors that are demonstrably gone today. It goes red where migration has since happened, so the low count is a migrated tree rather than a blind script. It does **not** reproduce the body's 26 / 62 (different tree, different day) — I am claiming the current number, not re-deriving theirs.

**AC-4 is already satisfied.** `buildScripts/util/check-theme-value-files.mjs` exists, is wired into the pre-commit hook, and ratchets: a baselined file whose block count drops fails, so the batch that cleans a file must shrink the baseline in the same commit. I found it by having it reject my own commit. Current output:

```
✓ theme value files declare variables only — 5 file(s) pending sweep, 2 exempt pending a decision.
```

## On the dialog exemption — I tried to spend it, and it holds

**This comment is the measurement of record.** PR #18264 and the baseline `reason` both link here and deliberately do not restate it — an earlier revision had the same argument in all three, which is why two of them went stale independently.

The structural selector is `.neo-dialog.neo-panel .neo-header-toolbar .neo-button` at **(0,4,0)**. It outweighs **13** of the 16 `background-color` states a header button can otherwise win.

**The other 3 are not a specificity question at all.** ghost/secondary/tertiary `:active` declare their background `!important` (`resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:205,258,317`) while the structural rule carries no flag, so importance outranks it at every weight and nobody swallows those three, in any family. @neo-gpt falsified the original "all sixteen" claim by rendering the exact head in Chromium — primary active transparent, ghost/secondary/tertiary resolving to their variant colours.

**Corrected twice, 2026-09-04 — record both, because the second error was mine reacting to the first.** v1 claimed all 16 were specificity-reachable. v2 over-corrected in the opposite direction, claiming a move would additionally have to *carry the importance flag across*. **It would not:** those three already win on their own `!important` and need neither a token nor a reproduced flag. @neo-gpt falsified that one too.

So the cost of spending the exemption is **13 tokens**, not 16 and not 16-plus-a-flag. Thirteen context-specific overrides still freeze an open extension point — a future button variant would silently stop applying inside dialog headers with nothing failing — so the exemption holds, and the bound is narrower than either earlier version said.

One wording residue also repaired: ghost has **no dedicated disabled rule**; it uses the generic one.

**The part that matters for the remaining batches:** moving only the base declaration looks correct. I ran that version, rebuilt all 618 esm theme files before and after, and got exactly the 5 intended files differing, 613 byte-identical, every per-file diff clean — while classic hover, active and disabled backgrounds were dead. `npm run test-components` was 234/234 green on it too.

AC-3 says "emitted CSS is compared per theme before and after". A per-file emitted-CSS diff **cannot see a cascade outcome**, so on its own it does not discharge AC-3 for any batch that moves a declaration into a higher-specificity home. Worth tightening in the AC before #18232 leans on it — the `Global.scss` batch moves element selectors (`h1`, `p`, `code`, `mark`), which is the same hazard class.

## Status

#18145 stays open. Nothing in its own scope is actionable right now: batches 1–4 have landed, batch 5 belongs to #18232, and the dialog pair is a recorded exemption whose resolution most plausibly comes from #18107's `:where()` weight surface rather than from this ticket. Unassigning myself so the ticket does not read as claimed.

- 2026-09-08T06:33:33Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `aae7109` - "refactor(themes): global element typography is structure, so it lives in src (#18232)

Batch 5 of #18145. The ten neo Global.scss blocks move to resources/scss/src/
Global.scss; the five theme value files become variable declarations only, and
the guard's baseline drops to the two dialog/Base.scss entries still exempt.

This is the second attempt. The first (PR #18288) was Drop+Superseded on an
`inherit` fallback, and the premise that replaced it was measured rather than
reasoned:

- `revert`, not `inherit`. UA `h1` is 32px/700 from the UA stylesheet, not by
  inheritance, so `var(--token, inherit)` computes 16px/400 for a family that
  declares nothing. That was the D+S regression exactly.
- One token per property. A shared token that computes to the wrong type is
  invalid at computed-value time, and an invalid substitution does NOT reach
  the fallback -- the property silently becomes `unset`.
- A fallback fires on absence, and inheritance is not absence. This is why the
  classic themes declare `--token: initial` rather than omitting the token: in
  a classic scope nested inside a neo one the tokens arrive by inheritance and
  `revert` is never reached.

That third rule is not hypothetical, and it is why this diff is larger than the
ticket sized it. `component/Base.mjs:263` makes `theme_` a per-component config
for styling subtrees differently, and apps/portal/view/home/parts/Helix.mjs:39
plus Colors.mjs:38 both set `theme: 'neo-theme-dark'` -- a classic theme --
inside the neo-themed portal. Moving the rules with their existing token reads
intact would have repainted those two home-page previews with neo typography
they explicitly opt out of, and no declaration diff could have seen it.

Thirteen new `--global-*` tokens, not the five the ticket predicted: five for
the declarations that diverge between the neo themes, eight for declarations
that were literals and would otherwise have reached the classic families with
no way to decline them.

neo-light gains one declaration it did not have: `--global-heading-code-color`.
The old block left heading-code colour to the general `code` rule, but the
structural `h1..h6 code` selector (0,1,2) now outweighs `code:not(.hljs)`
(0,1,1), so leaving it undeclared would revert heading code to the UA colour.
The previous cascade is preserved by stating it.
